inventory.visualPurpose: Fuel-source dominance across duration of exercise
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Fig 7: % maximal energy by source (y, 0 to 100%) vs duration of exercise (x: 2 sec, 10 sec, 1 min, 2 hr) — five curves with legend: stored ATP (starts 100%, spent within seconds), creatine phosphate (peaks between 2 and 10 sec), anaerobic metabolism (peaks near 1 min), aerobic metabolism (rises continuously, dominant after ~1 min), overall performance (100% at start, flat to ~10 sec, declines to low plateau by 2 hr).

inventory.visualPurpose: Stored energy decline across weeks of starvation
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: Fig 8: stored energy (kJ) (y, ticks 12, 10, 8, 6, 4, 2, 0) vs weeks of starvation (x, 0-8) — three solid curves: protein (starts 12, slow decline accelerating after week 6 to ~5 at week 8), fat (starts 12, near-linear decline to ~1 at week 8), carbohydrate (starts ~0.5, at zero within week 1). Invisible text-layer artifacts present (duplicated right-axis '100% / % Maximal energy by source', stray '2 sec') — InDesign leftovers, not visible in print.

inventory.sourceBook: First Aid for the USMLE Step 1 2026
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The states table: priorities banner (supply sufficient glucose to the brain and RBCs and preserve protein); fed state (glycolysis + aerobic respiration; insulin stores TG/glycogen + protein synthesis); fasting (hepatic glycogenolysis major, GNG + adipose FFA minor; glucagon/epinephrine); starvation days 1-3 (glycogenolysis, adipose FFA, glucose-to-FFA shift, GNG from lactate/alanine/glycerol/propionyl-CoA from odd-chain FFA; glycogen depleted after day 1; RBCs lack mitochondria); starvation after day 3 (adipose stores, ketones main brain source; depleted stores → vital protein degradation → organ failure and death; excess stores determine survival time).
